transcript.message: Holt has given you one minute to inspect the linkage. Please look, but don't touch the catch or promise a repair. When the minute is up, tell me exactly what's binding.

*I kneel beside the cart and trace the linkage with my eyes, keeping both hands clear of the catch. After a careful circuit I rise and dust off my knees.*

“I can't honestly name a single binding point. The frame is still wedged and the cart is holding itself rigid around the tree, but I won't pretend the inspection proved more than that.”

Thank you for being honest. If the cart is protecting the tree, what if we lift the tree off together and set it somewhere safe and visible? With nothing left to protect, perhaps the cart will stop bracing. Would you supervise that?

Binding GM ruling: persuasion major_success; natural 3, modifier 17, total 20, DC 15. Rowan accepts the practical compromise and agrees to supervise the crew lifting the tree from the cart and setting it down safely where the cart can see it. Rowan cannot promise how Nine Furrows will react, and the move has not happened yet. Preserve the distinction between agreeing to the attempt and observing its result; do not roll again.

*My shoulders ease as I look from the potted tree to the crew.*

“Yes. That's a practical compromise. I'll supervise the lift and make sure the tree is set down safely and kept in view. I can't speak for all of Nine Furrows, and we won't assume it worked until we see what the cart does with the tree away from it.”
Good. Let's do it now, carefully. Count the crew in, lift the tree clear, and set it down where it will be safe.

*I place the crew around the pot, check every grip, and raise three fingers.* “On three. Keep it level, and mind the roots. One, two, three.” *Together we lift the tree clear of the cart and carry it a few paces to an open patch beside the entrance.*
Easy now. Is the tree down safely? What did the cart do once it was clear?

*I give the crew a firm nod and count them through the lift, guiding the pot clear of the cart without letting it tip. Once the tree is set upright in a safe, visible spot, I turn back to the wheels and linkage.*

“It’s down safely. The cart stopped bracing as soon as the tree was clear—look, the wheels eased back and it rolled out of the service passage. The entrance is open.”
